sections.title: The Prophecy Against Egypt
observations: Ezekiel 30 begins with a strong declaration of judgment against Egypt, emphasizing the impending disaster that will befall the nation. This prophecy is significant as it reflects God's sovereignty over all nations, not just Israel. The imagery of a sword and the mention of various nations serve to illustrate the widespread impact of this judgment.

The chapter highlights the role of Egypt as a major power in the ancient world and its eventual downfall. This serves as a reminder of the transient nature of earthly kingdoms and the ultimate authority of God.

sections.title: The Day of the Lord
observations: The text transitions to a description of the 'Day of the Lord,' a theme prevalent in prophetic literature. This day signifies a time of reckoning and divine intervention, where God will execute judgment not only on Egypt but also on other nations that have opposed Him.
The mention of various cities and regions within Egypt underscores the comprehensive nature of this judgment, indicating that no part of Egypt will escape the consequences of their actions.

importantVerses.commentary: For the day is near, the day of the Lord is near; it will be a day of clouds, a time of doom for the nations.
Thus will I execute judgments on Egypt, and they shall know that I am the Lord.

questions: What does the judgment against Egypt reveal about God's character and His relationship with nations?
How does the concept of the 'Day of the Lord' shape our understanding of God's justice and sovereignty?
In what ways can we see parallels between the judgment of Egypt and the judgments described in the New Testament?
